 Golden Knights, Wild Swap Jeremy Davies, Gerald Mayhew
 By Brennan McClain |
 at November 16, 2026 8:30 pm 
 The Minnesota Wild and Vegas Golden Knights have swapped out a pair of depth players. The Golden Knights traded defenseman Jeremy Davies to the Wild, and the Wild sent forward Gerald Mayhew to the Golden Knights organization.
 Although it doesn’t change anything, these are technically different transactions. Because Mayhew is on an AHL contract, it was the Iowa Wild who officially dealt him to the Henderson Silver Knights for future considerations. The Wild already announced that Davies will report to Des Moines.
 Once a standout defenseman at Northeastern University, Davies, 29, has failed to put it all together in the NHL. The Ste-Anne-de-Bellevue, QC, native was originally drafted by the New Jersey Devils with the 192nd overall pick (seventh round) in the 2016 NHL Draft. Davies eventually signed a two-year, entry-level contract with the Devils, but was traded to the Nashville Predators a few months later in the P.K. Subban trade.
 Beginning his professional career shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic, Davies never gathered any momentum with Nashville, or anywhere else, for that matter. Now into his eighth professional campaign, Davies has blossomed into a solid AHL defenseman with very little NHL experience. Before joining his new club, Davies scored 54 goals and 225 points in 415 AHL contests with a +55 rating. In the NHL, he has registered three assists in 23 appearances since the 2020-21 season.
 Still, whether he’s in Iowa or Minnesota, Davies should have a positive influence on the organization. Minnesota has dealt with multiple injuries to their blue line this season, and could certainly use more depth if they aren’t out of the woods yet. Meanwhile, if he stays in Iowa, he could help them end a years-long postseason drought.
 On the other side of the transaction, Mayhew will join the sixth organization of his career. An AHL-only player at this stage of his career, the 33-year-old veteran has not appeared in the NHL since the 2021-22 campaign, when he scored six goals in 25 games for the Philadelphia Flyers and five goals in 15 games with the Anaheim Ducks after a mid-season waiver claim.
 Since then, Mayhew has spent the last five years exclusively in the AHL. Last season, his first in the Wild organization since the 2020-21 campaign, Mayhew had one of the better individual seasons of his career, registering 22 goals and 42 points in 60 games with a -16 rating.
 The pair of trades will drop the Golden Knights to 47 active contracts and increase Minnesota’s to 44.
